meta.scope: Mexico batch 11 — Monterrey metropolitan area (Nuevo León entity + Monterrey + key metro municipalities). Completes the three largest / most developed metro zooms (CDMX, Guadalajara, Monterrey).

candidates.title: Nuevo León (entidad federativa) — core statistical identity
candidates.description: Nuevo León as a federal entity: population, high economic contribution (especially manufacturing), formal employment, public finances, justice and the full set of national programmes disaggregated to the state. Parent node for the Monterrey metropolitan municipalities.
candidates.notes: One of the most industrialised and competitive states. Second place nationally in economic census production in recent results; Monterrey metro is the primary engine. Bridge node between national series and the municipal layer.

candidates.title: Zona Metropolitana de Monterrey (ZMM) — metropolitan statistical profile
candidates.publisher: INEGI / CONAPO / SEDATU / local planning bodies
candidates.region: Nuevo León — Zona Metropolitana de Monterrey
candidates.description: Statistical identity of the Monterrey metropolitan area (commonly 16+ municipalities). Population ~5.3–5.4 million (2020). Regularly referenced in national metropolitan delineations and in state/local economic and demographic analysis.
candidates.notes: Largest metro in northern Mexico and one of the three primary metro zooms. National delineations (SEDATU/CONAPO/INEGI) and economic censuses treat it as a coherent statistical unit. High labour mobility across municipalities is a defining feature.

candidates.title: Municipio de Monterrey — statistical and administrative profile
candidates.description: Core municipality of the metro (~1.14 million in 2020). Major economic contributor (recent economic census ranked it among the top municipalities nationally by production). Profile from census, CNGMD, DENUE, IMSS, economic census and local planning documents.
candidates.notes: Primary municipal node for the northern industrial capital. Economic census results repeatedly highlight Monterrey’s outsized contribution to national and state production.

candidates.title: Municipio de Guadalupe (Nuevo León) — statistical profile
candidates.description: Large, dense municipality in the Monterrey metro. One of the most populous in the state after Monterrey itself. Covered by the standard national disaggregations (census, CNGMD, DENUE, IMSS).
candidates.notes: Second major municipal node in the ZMM. High density and large population make it a natural companion to Monterrey.

candidates.title: Municipio de Apodaca — statistical profile
candidates.description: Major industrial and population municipality in the Monterrey metro. Frequently ranks high in economic census production shares within Nuevo León (often second after Monterrey).
candidates.notes: Key industrial municipality of the metro. Economic census results regularly list Apodaca among the top contributors to state and national production.

candidates.title: Municipio de San Nicolás de los Garza — statistical profile
candidates.region: Nuevo León — San Nicolás de los Garza
candidates.description: Dense, established municipality in the core of the Monterrey metro. High population density; standard national statistical coverage.
referenced_by: Census, CNGMD, DENUE, IMSS municipal series
candidates.notes: Core metro municipality with high density. Completes the main traditional core alongside Monterrey, Guadalupe and Apodaca.

candidates.title: Municipio de San Pedro Garza García — statistical profile
candidates.region: Nuevo León — San Pedro Garza García
candidates.description: Affluent, high-income municipality in the Monterrey metro, known for elevated socioeconomic indicators. Covered by national disaggregations and local reporting.
candidates.notes: Distinct socioeconomic profile within the metro (higher incomes, different service and housing patterns). Useful contrast node to the larger industrial municipalities.

candidates.title: Poder Judicial del Estado de Nuevo León — statistical reporting
candidates.publisher: Tribunal Superior de Justicia / Poder Judicial de Nuevo León
candidates.description: State judiciary statistical outputs (caseload, organs, resources, performance indicators). Visible through the national CNIJE and through local transparency and labour reports of the Nuevo León judiciary.
candidates.notes: Local judiciary maintains public statistical snapshots (judges, magistrates, hearings, filings, resolutions). CNIJE places Nuevo León among states with relatively low judges-per-capita but competitive performance on certain clearance indicators. Completes the three-metro judicial coverage (CDMX, Jalisco, Nuevo León).

candidates.title: IMSS formal employment by municipality (Nuevo León / Monterrey metro)
candidates.description: Municipal disaggregation of IMSS-affiliated employment for Nuevo León municipalities, especially the dense set of municipalities that form the Monterrey metro.
candidates.notes: Same architecture as the Jalisco municipal IMSS series. Critical for tracking formal employment across the industrial metro.

candidates.title: Censos Económicos — resultados municipales (producción y unidades económicas)
candidates.description: Municipal-level results of the Economic Censuses (units, employment, production). Particularly valuable for ranking municipalities such as Monterrey, Apodaca and others by economic contribution.
candidates.notes: The economic census is already in the national inventory; this node emphasises the municipal tabulations that enable the metro and municipality zooms (e.g. Monterrey’s high national rank by production). Recurring every five years with provisional and definitive releases.

proposed_edges.basis: Municipal production and establishment counts that underpin Monterrey’s economic ranking come from the Economic Census municipal results.
Apodaca’s high share of state production is documented in Economic Census municipal tabulations.
The metropolitan area is a statistical aggregation of municipalities within Nuevo León.
State judiciary statistics feed into and are consistent with the national CNIJE.
Municipal IMSS series are geographic disaggregations of the national formal-employment statistics.
